# fivenines_zfs_pools (Data Source)

The per-pool health rows behind the instance's storage view -- which pool is degraded, how far the resilver got, and what the last scrub found.

THE NULL-VS-ZERO RULE IS THE POINT of these columns. `scrub_errors` null means unknown (never scrubbed, resilver in progress, or `zpool status` unavailable) while `0` means a scrub completed clean -- reading null as 0 turns "nobody has ever checked" into "verified healthy". `degraded_vdevs` / `resilver_progress` / `vdev_tree` are null when `zpool status` was unavailable that tick, and `health` may still be present (it comes from `zpool list`), so "DEGRADED with a null `degraded_vdevs`" is a real row: degraded, extent unknown.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "fivenines_zfs_pools" "all" {
  instance_id = fivenines_instance.storage.id
}

output "degraded_pools" {
  value = [for p in data.fivenines_zfs_pools.all.zfs_pools : p.name if p.problem]
}

# scrub_errors is null when nobody has ever checked and 0 when a scrub
# completed clean. Reading the null as 0 turns "unverified" into "verified".
output "pools_never_scrubbed" {
  value = [
    for p in data.fivenines_zfs_pools.all.zfs_pools :
    p.name if p.scrub_errors == null
  ]
}

output "tank_vdev_tree" {
  value = {
    for p in data.fivenines_zfs_pools.all.zfs_pools :
    p.name => jsondecode(p.vdev_tree) if p.vdev_tree != null
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID the rows belong to.

### Optional

- `health` (String) Filter by the raw zpool health string. One of: `ONLINE`, `DEGRADED`, `FAULTED`, `OFFLINE`, `REMOVED`, `UNAVAIL`, `SUSPENDED`. A state ZFS adds later is still returned unfiltered, it just cannot be selected by name.
- `q` (String) Case-insensitive substring match on the pool name.
- `stale` (Boolean) Freshness filter over the collector's 10-minute sync window. `false` returns only rows the agent refreshed inside it -- the set you may read as CURRENT state; `true` returns the rest. The two values partition the collection (a row that never synced counts as stale). Omit for both.
- `updated_since` (String) Return only rows whose `updated_at` is at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Inclusive, so a row updated in the same instant as the cursor comes back rather than falling through the gap. The ingester touches `updated_at` on every agent tick, so this is a freshness filter rather than a change feed, and there are no tombstones: a row the agent stops reporting is deleted.

### Read-Only

- `collector` (Attributes) Why the row list looks the way it does. Read this before treating an empty list as a clean bill of health: `[]` alone cannot distinguish "this host genuinely runs none" from "the collector is switched off" (which deletes the rows) or "this agent is too old to report them". (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--collector))
- `zfs_pools` (Attributes List) The rows the collector reported. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--zfs_pools))

<a id="nestedatt--collector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `collector`

Read-Only:

- `blocked_reason` (String) The agent's own explanation, where it sent one. Null otherwise.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the operator has this collector switched on for the instance. Switching it off deletes the rows, so `false` fully explains an empty list.
- `last_reported_at` (String) The instance's last agent check-in -- not this collector's. It separates "this collector went quiet" (rows stale, instance reporting) from "the whole agent went quiet" (both). Per-row freshness is each row's `last_synced_at`.
- `name` (String) The collector these rows come from.
- `pending` (Boolean) Enabled, and the agent knows the feature, but the capability is not satisfied yet (missing binary, missing permission). The rows are legitimately absent and may appear on a later tick.
- `supported` (Boolean) Whether this agent can collect these rows -- its own capability verdict where it reports one, its version otherwise. `false` alongside `enabled` means the instance was asked for something it cannot deliver. Read it as "the agent has not said it cannot": the config-driven collectors (haproxy, rabbitmq, php_fpm, wireguard) have no version floor, so an agent predating one still reports `true` with an empty list.
- `unavailable_reason` (String) Why `supported` is false: `host_lacks_feature` (the agent probed and reported it cannot) or `agent_outdated` (the agent predates the release that collects these rows). Null when supported.


<a id="nestedatt--zfs_pools"></a>
### Nested Schema for `zfs_pools`

Read-Only:

- `alloc_bytes` (Number) Bytes allocated. **Null means unavailable**, not 0.
- `capacity_percent` (Number) Percent of the pool allocated. **Null means `zpool status` was unavailable**, not 0.
- `created_at` (String) When this row was first recorded. This is when the agent first happened to report it, not anything an operator would recognize.
- `data_errors` (String) The raw `errors:` line from `zpool status`.
- `dedup_ratio` (Number) Deduplication ratio. **Null means unavailable**, not 0.
- `degraded_vdevs` (Number) Every unhealthy node, intermediate vdevs AND leaves (one faulted disk in a mirror counts 2), so use it as a `> 0` signal, never as "N disks failed". **Null means `zpool status` was unavailable this tick**, not zero.
- `fragmentation` (Number) Percent.
- `free_bytes` (Number) Bytes free. **Null means unavailable**, not 0.
- `health` (String) The raw zpool health string, verbatim. Null means the tick carried no health at all -- which is NOT "ONLINE". A state ZFS adds later keeps its string here with a null `health_code`.
- `health_code` (Number) Stable 0 ONLINE .. 6 SUSPENDED enum. Null when `health` is unrecognized.
- `host_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID this row belongs to.
- `id` (Number) Row identifier.
- `last_synced_at` (String) Server arrival time of the tick that last refreshed this row (never the agent's clock). Null when the row has never synced.
- `name` (String) The pool name, e.g. `tank`. This is the row identity.
- `problem` (Boolean) Health present and not ONLINE. A null health reads false: unknown is never a problem signal.
- `resilver_progress` (Number) Percent. `0.0` means BOTH "not resilvering" and "resilver just started, no percent printed yet" -- only a positive value proves one is running, which is what `resilvering` reports. **Null means `zpool status` was unavailable.**
- `resilvering` (Boolean) Whether a resilver is running. The authoritative answer: `resilver_progress` reads `0.0` both for "not resilvering" and for "just started, no percent printed yet".
- `scrub_errors` (Number) **Null means unknown** -- never scrubbed, resilver in progress, or `zpool status` unavailable. `0` means a scrub completed clean. Reading null as 0 turns "nobody has ever checked" into "verified healthy".
- `scrub_verdict` (String) `clean`, `N errors`, or null when `scrub_errors` is unknown.
- `size_bytes` (Number) Pool size in bytes. **Null means unavailable**, not 0.
- `stale` (Boolean) True when the agent has not refreshed this row inside the 10-minute window.
- `state_changed_at` (String) When `health` last flipped.
- `state_detail` (String) Human summary, e.g. `DEGRADED -- resilvering (42.1% done)`.
- `updated_at` (String) When this row was last written. The ingester touches it on every agent tick, so it is a freshness stamp rather than a change feed.
- `vdev_tree` (String) Scrubbed diagnostic tree -- which vdev or disk is faulted. **Null means `zpool status` was unavailable.** Section devices (logs/cache/spares/special) appear BOTH nested in `children` and in their own section list; that is deliberate, so do not count them twice. JSON-encoded; decode with `jsondecode()`.
- `zfs_version` (String) The ZFS version string the host reported, e.g. `zfs-2.2.2-1`. Null when not reported.
